claim: Driving distance from Luxembourg City to Trier is roughly 49 km, about a 46-minute drive — Moutfort sits east of Luxembourg City so trip is similar (~45 km)
quote: The driving distance between Luxembourg and Trier is 30.41 mi (48.93 km), with a driving time of approximately 0h 46min.

claim: Trier's Roman monuments, the Cathedral of St Peter and the Liebfrauenkirche are collectively inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site
quote: Roman Monuments, Cathedral of St Peter and Church of Our Lady in Trier

claim: The Porta Nigra is a 2nd-century Roman fortified gate flanked by two semi-circular four-storey towers and is Trier's signature landmark
quote: The Porta Nigra is an enormous fortified gate built of large stones, flanked by two semi-circular four-storey towers, and is a unique achievement of 2nd century Roman architecture.

claim: The Constantine Basilica (Konstantin-Basilika) in Trier is 32m x 61m and 36m tall, and is the largest surviving Roman building without internal columns
quote: 32m x 61m and 36m tall, doesn't have a single pillar in it, making it the largest building without columns, surviving since Roman Era

claim: Trier Cathedral is the oldest cathedral in Germany, with its core nave built of Roman brick in the early 4th century under Constantine
quote: Trier Cathedral is the oldest cathedral in Germany... central part of the nave was built of Roman brick in the early fourth century

claim: The Liebfrauenkirche, adjacent to Trier Cathedral, is the earliest church built in French High Gothic style outside France (1230–1260)
quote: the earliest church built in French High Gothic style outside France

claim: Karl Marx's birthplace at Brückenstraße 10 in Trier operates as a museum run by the Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung
Karl-Marx-Haus summer hours (15 March – 14 November) are daily 10 am–6 pm; winter hours close on Mondays; admission €7 adult
quote: Summer opening hours (March 15 – November 14): Monday – Sunday: 10 am – 6 pm. Winter opening hours (November 15 – March 14): Tuesday – Sunday: 10 am – 6 pm.

claim: The Schengen Museum sits at the Luxembourg-Germany-France tripoint and the original MS Princesse Marie-Astrid boat where the 1985 agreement was signed is docked on site with a visitable upper-deck signing room
quote: The original vessel where the historic agreement was signed on June 14, 1985, is docked at the museum site. Visitors can board the upper deck's signing room

claim: The Three-Borders Monument erected in 1997 has three steel columns bearing stars representing the original Schengen signatory countries
quote: Erected in 1997, the monument features three tall steel columns, each bearing a star to represent the first signatory countries of the Schengen Agreement

claim: The Roman Villa Nennig at Römerstraße 11, 66706 Perl, houses a 160 m² mosaic of over 3 million tiles depicting gladiator and animal-hunt scenes, open March–November
quote: one of the most beautiful and largest examples of Roman mosaic art of the 2nd and 3rd century... 160-square-meter floor contains over 3 million tiles

claim: The Nennig mosaic was discovered in 1852 by a farmer and remains in situ, an unusual survival for Roman mosaics north of the Alps
quote: The mosaic at the Roman villa in Nennig

claim: The Upper Mosel cycle path runs from Perl to Nittel along the German Moselle bank through vineyards with no gradients, suited to relaxed wine-village hopping
quote: Mosel Cycle Path Section 1: From Perl to Nittel

claim: Nittel is the standout wine village of the Upper Mosel with numerous wineries, wine taverns and inns clustered in one small town
The Saarschleife treetop walk and viewpoint near Mettlach is about a 36 km / 42-minute drive from Luxembourg City — outside the strict 30 km radius but reachable in under an hour
quote: the distance between Baumwipfelpfad Saarschleife and Luxembourg is 25 miles (24.2 miles by road). The fastest way to get from Baumwipfelpfad Saarschleife to Luxembourg is to drive, which takes 42 minutes

claim: The Saarschleife is a water gap where the Saar carves a hairpin through quartzite; the Cloef viewpoint sits ~180 m above the river and the Baumwipfelpfad treetop walk opened July 2016
quote: a water gap carved by the Saar River through a quartzite layer
